subject: physics_2
question_text: Which gates are called universal gates.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. The book (p.55) answers only with the two names; the reason for the name 'universal' is added here because a 2-mark question is unlikely to be paid in full for two words.

recall_prompt: Name the two universal gates and say what makes them universal.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two gates
lines: The NAND gate and the NOR gate are
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both names are needed; one alone is half the answer.
steps.why: The two names are the whole marked answer in the book, so they must be written first and written together.
common_mistakes: Naming only NAND. NOR is universal as well.
Naming AND and OR. Those two cannot build a NOT gate by themselves.

recall.must_convey: That NAND and NOR are the universal gates.
accept: the NAND gate and the NOR gate

steps.memory_tip: Both universal gates end in a bubble: NAND and NOR.

steps.label: Why universal
steps.mark_note: Any gate can be built from them
lines: They are called universal because every
other logic gate — NOT, AND, OR — can be
built using NAND gates alone, or using
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 'Alone' is the word that matters: one type of gate is enough.
steps.why: The word universal is not about being common; it is about being sufficient. A single NAND gate with both inputs joined is a NOT gate, and a NAND followed by that NOT gate is an AND gate, so the whole set of gates can be made from one type.
common_mistakes: Saying they are universal because they are used most often. The reason is that they can build every other gate.
Saying NAND and NOR together build the others. Each one alone is enough.

recall.must_convey: That every other gate can be built from NAND gates alone or NOR gates alone.
accept: any gate can be made from them
NOT AND OR can be built with NAND alone
one type of gate is enough
reject: output is high only when both inputs are low

steps.memory_tip: Universal = enough on its own. One gate type builds the rest.

insider_note: The book answers with two names only. Add one line saying why they are called universal — a 2-mark question rarely pays full marks for two words.
